4. The sharp version: crawl → probe → close the delta
This is the part that makes it a product rather than a generator.

blocks.text:
1. CRAWL      the domain. Build a graph of what the site actually claims.
2. PROBE      the engines. Ask ChatGPT/Perplexity/Gemini/AIO about this brand
              and its category. Record what they say and what they cite.
3. DIFF       the two.
                • facts the site states that the models don't know
                • things the models say about the brand that are WRONG
                • questions the models answer with a competitor cited
                • claims the site makes with no supporting page to cite
4. GENERATE   content that closes exactly those gaps, grounded in step 1.
5. RE-PROBE   in 30 days. Did the gap close?

Domain-only input means no credentials, so v1 is generate + export (markdown / HTML / PDF) with CMS detected from the crawl and the right handoff offered. Publishing integrations (WordPress ≈ 40% of the web, Webflow, Shopify, Ghost) are the obvious v2 and the thing the incumbents already have. Not a blocker, but don't underestimate it.
Anyone can paste any domain. Gate it: crawl + gap report is cheap and becomes the free tier; generation is expensive and is the paid action. That split also happens to be the right funnel.
You have no volume numbers from a domain alone — but for GEO the unit of demand is a
, not a keyword with a volume figure, and the question set comes from the probe step. The missing keyword data is only a problem if you're building an SEO tool. Build the GEO tool.

This maps onto tooling that already exists in this portfolio more than incidentally: crawl → build a claim graph → extract edges → find structural gaps → trace every generated statement back along an evidence path. That is Graphonomous's shape (knowledge graph, edge extraction, evidence-path tracing, belief revision when a crawl contradicts a prior crawl). Worth evaluating as the engine rather than building claim-graph infrastructure from scratch.
as in alchemy/algebra/algorithm is a coherent, defensible logic, and "transmute what you already have into gold" is a genuinely good brand story that the product actually delivers on.

Remaining real issue: it fails the radio test — said aloud, most people won't spell it right, and some will hear "AI keyword." Mitigate by making the alchemy framing loud and immediate on the page (the wordmark, the metaphor, the copy) so the
reads as intentional within two seconds.
